short: Britain's first woman prime minister, and the one who remade its economy.
full:
Margaret Thatcher won three general elections and served eleven and a half years, longer than any other prime minister of the twentieth century. Her governments broke with the post-war consensus: exchange controls abolished in 1979, council houses sold to their tenants, income tax rates cut, trade union law progressively tightened, and British Telecom, British Gas, British Airways and the water and electricity industries sold to shareholders.

Unemployment passed three million and manufacturing output contracted sharply. She recaptured the Falklands in 1982, survived the Brighton bombing in 1984, defeated the year-long miners' strike in 1985, and worked with Reagan and Gorbachev through the closing years of the Cold War. The community charge, or poll tax, provoked riots and mass non-payment, and her hostility to European integration split her cabinet. Her own MPs forced her out in November 1990, and she left Downing Street in tears.
